item.title: ‘No more playstation’ – Anthony Joshua welcomes baby girl
item.description: Nigerian-British boxing champion, Anthony Joshua, has announced the birth of his second child, a girl, noting that there is no more time for PlayStation or FIFA for him. Joshua and his childhood sweetheart, Nicole Osbourne, welcomed their daughter on November 14, 2026. The pair also have an 11-year-old son, Joseph. The former two-time unified heavyweight champion revealed this in an interview with The Sun , which gained attention on Thursday, said having a daughter would help him better understand women and how to support them. “Now I’ve got a daughter, I will get an insight and a bit more understanding of what it means to be a woman, and how I can be supportive. My daughter will give me firsthand experience of a woman’s power,” he said. Joshua disclosed that the family had yet to settle on a name for the newborn, but described her as his princess. “I’ve spoken to all the women in my family, and it’s amazing the amount of support that women give each other. We haven’t given her a name yet, but she’s my Princess,” he added. The 36 year old boxer described the birth as a huge blessing, revealing that he deliberately avoided finding out the baby’s sex during the pregnancy. “It’s been amazing, a big blessing and I can’t believe I’m a girl dad. I didn’t want to find the sex out during the pregnancy,” Joshua said. He also joked about how having a daughter could change some of the activities he shares with his son. “I love boys but as soon as I found out we had a little girl I said, ‘No more Fifa, no more motorbiking, no more PlayStation!’” he said. “I’m going to do it all, so you might see me with some eyeshadow on, some nail polish on, drinking some tea in a doll’s playhouse and just trying to do the right thing by her, you know?” he said. He also spoke about the responsibilities of caring for a newborn, saying he was prepared to change nappies and go through the demands of raising a baby again. “I will change nappies, I’ve gotta go through all that stinky bum time again!” he added. The development comes as Joshua prepares for a reported December 11 showdown with fellow British heavyweight boxer Tyson Fury. item.title: Oil resumption: KAGOTE insists Ogoni people must ratify FG’s MoU
item.description: …Group welcomes Tinubu’s intervention on Eleme section of East-West Road By Daniel Abia, Port Harcourt The leadership of KAGOTE, comprising Khana, Gokana, Tai and Eleme local government areas of Rivers State, has insisted that the proposed Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) between the Federal Government and the Ogoni people on the resumption of oil exploration in Ogoniland must be ratified by the people before it is signed. The group said the contents of the proposed agreement must be presented to the Ogoni people for approval to secure their mandate and ensure the legitimacy of the process. KAGOTE President, Chief Lesi Ma-ol, stated this in a statement, explaining that it had been agreed that congresses should be convened in Khana, Gokana, Tai and Eleme by their duly elected local government chairmen to consider and ratify the proposed agreement. He said the arrangement would address concerns over the legality and legitimacy of the Ogoni Dialogue Committee (ODC) and provide a platform for the people to approve the MoU with the Federal Government. Ma-ol stressed the need for unity within the ODC, insisting that no individual or group of members should sign any agreement on behalf of the committee without its collective approval and ratification by the congresses. “We consider the unity of the ODC as essential, as such it was resolved that we shall sign as a collective. No member or group of members shall, by themselves, sign any document on behalf of the ODC that has not been adopted by the ODC and approved/ratified by the congresses. “We are totally in support of the resumption of oil and gas exploration in Ogoniland. We are committed to ensuring that the necessary foundations are properly laid. We want a resumption that brings peace, security, employment, economic opportunities, environmental responsibility and sustainable development to our land,” he said. The KAGOTE president said President Bola Tinubu initiated the peace process with good intentions, adding that the group was committed to doing everything possible to ensure its success. He, however, said a sustainable outcome must be built on trust, inclusiveness, transparency and the legitimate mandate of the Ogoni people. Ma-ol explained that KAGOTE was currently involved in harmonising the Federal Government’s response to the demands of the Ogoni people, a process expected to culminate in the proposed MoU. He said the group had consistently advocated the implementation of confidence-building measures agreed upon with the Federal Government, including employment opportunities, schools, hospital renovations and other development projects, alongside the Eleme section of the East-West Road. According to him, several of the projects remain stalled, with their levels of completion ranging from zero to about 40 per cent. item.title: Mera denies defection rumour to APC in Kebbi
item.description: By Haruna Aliyu, Birnin Kebbi The African Democratic Congress (ADC) senatorial candidate for Kebbi North, Alhaji Ibrahim Muhammad Mera, has dismissed reports circulating on social media that he has defected to the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) in Kebbi State. Mera, in a statement signed by his Director-General, Media, Garba Muhammad Yeldu, on Thursday, said he had neither met nor held discussions with any APC official or member over a possible defection. He described the reports as fabricated, alleging that they were being circulated by individuals seeking to create confusion and distract him from pursuing his senatorial ambition under the ADC. Mera acknowledged that political parties were experiencing internal challenges but insisted that the crisis within the ADC would not make him abandon the party. He said the APC also had its internal disagreements, adding that he remained focused on his political ambition and the pursuit of the Kebbi North senatorial seat. The ADC candidate urged his supporters and constituents to disregard the reports, describing them as products of the rumour peddlers’ imagination. He also appealed to them to remain calm, peaceful and law-abiding while continuing to support the ADC. “I have never for once thought or made attempts to leave ADC. I remain focused and unrelenting in the pursuit of my mandate in my party,” he said. Mera warned those behind the reports to desist from spreading what he described as false information and assured his supporters of his continued loyalty to the ADC. item.title: Leicester split with sponsor after row over porn actor partnership
item.description: Leicester City have parted ways with front-of-shirt sponsor BC Game following a fan backlash over the gambling firm’s appointment of a porn actor as an ambassador. The crypto gaming company, which became a sponsor for the former Premier League champions in 2024, named Eva Elfie as a brand ambassador earlier this month. Fan group the Foxes Trust stated on November 4, stating their dismay over the partnership. “Both gambling and pornography can have devastating impacts on people’s lives, in particular young people,” it said. “Partnerships like these bring these two worlds to a larger audience and, by association, link them to Leicester City. Is this who we are now?” Leicester, who now play in the third tier of English football, issued a statement on Wednesday saying the club and BC Game had “reached a mutual agreement to conclude our commercial partnership with immediate effect”. “The decision follows constructive discussions between both parties in recent days, during which we recognised our differing commercial priorities moving forward,” it said. The club thanked BC Game for the “constructive approach taken in reaching this agreement”. The statement did not refer to the supporters’ stated objections. Leicester shocked the sporting world when they won the Premier League in 2016, following up with an FA Cup triumph five years later. But the club has fallen on hard times in recent years and are currently 11th in League One. item.title: ‘Enjoy the ride’- Pierce Brosnan tells Pattinson, new James Bond 007
item.description: Irish actor Pierce Brosnan, who once played the role of the world’s most famous spy, has welcomed Robert Pattinson to the “world of Bond”, urging him to “enjoy the ride”. “You are going to be magnificent,” Brosnan wrote in a post on Instagram, under a black-and-white picture of Pattinson dressed as secret agent James Bond in a tuxedo and brandishing a hand-gun. “It has been a joy to watch you create a remarkable body of work and to go from strength to strength,” he added. Brosnan played Bond in four films from 1995 to 2002, including “GoldenEye” and “Tomorrow Never Dies”, before handing over to Daniel Craig. After months of speculation, Amazon MGM Studios on Monday named British actor Pattinson as the seventh performer to step into the coveted 007 role, replacing Craig. Pattinson became a global pop culture phenomenon with his vampire role in the “Twilight” saga before being cast as Batman. He also starred alongside Brosnan in the 2010 romantic drama “Remember Me”. Brosnan signed off his message with “Gra Mor, Pierce” — Irish for “big love”. Another Bond alum, George Lazenby, who played the agent in the 1969 film “On Her Majesty’s Secret Service”, said on social media: “Robert, welcome to the most exclusive club in the world.” Craig, who played Bond in five films from 2006 to 2021, has yet to react to Pattinson stepping into his shoes. item.title: Police rescue 15 kidnapped victims in Kogi forest after gun battle
item.description: By Boluwaji Obahopo, Lokoja The Kogi State Police Command has rescued 15 kidnapped victims from a kidnappers’ den in Magaru Forest, Kakun-Kabba, following a fierce gun battle between security operatives and the abductors. The victims, comprising men, women and children, were rescued in the early hours of Wednesday, November 18, during an intelligence-led joint security operation involving the police, military, forest guards and local security outfits. The Commissioner of Police, Kogi State Command, CP Naziru Bello Kankarofi, disclosed this on Thursday while briefing journalists at the Police Headquarters in Lokoja. Bello Kankarofi said the operation was conducted on his directive, adding that the joint security team stormed the forest and engaged the kidnappers in a fierce gun battle. According to him, the superior firepower of the security operatives forced the criminals to retreat, with some of them sustaining varying degrees of gunshot injuries. He said, “During the operation, the joint team advanced into the forest and engaged the kidnappers in a fierce gun battle. The superior firepower of the security operatives forced the criminals to retreat, with some sustaining varying degrees of gunshot injuries.” The rescued victims were identified as Okuma Terlum, 47; Ojo Deborah, 23; Samuel Danjuma, three; Faith Raphael, 21; Emmanuella Raphael, three; Donald Tor, 31; Joseph Jonathan, 20; Tergu Joseph, 15; Samuel Joseph, eight; Engr. Joseph Adebija, 58; Lois Abiodun, 50; Chuks Obiakor, 45; Ola Olufemi, 58; Ankpe Godwin, 23; and Kuhwa Solomon, 25. The police commissioner also disclosed that two other female victims, identified simply as Joy and Nwakan, escaped from their abductors during the initial encounter in which the victims were taken captive. He further revealed that the security team came under another ambush by members of the criminal gang while conveying the rescued victims out of the forest. However, he said the operatives successfully repelled the attack and brought all 15 victims out safely. The victims, who reportedly endured considerable physical and psychological distress during their captivity, were subsequently debriefed and taken to St. John’s Catholic Hospital, Kabba, for medical attention. Although no arrests had been made as of the time of the briefing, the commissioner said actionable intelligence had been generated, while investigations were ongoing to track down the fleeing kidnappers and identify their sponsors. He commended the participating security agencies and local security outfits for their courage, resilience and collaboration, assuring residents of the command’s commitment to sustaining coordinated operations against kidnapping and other violent crimes. The operation involved personnel of the Kabba Area Command, Kabba ‘A’ Division, Iyara Division, Ekerin-Adde Division, Ayetoro-Gbede Division, Violent Crime Response Unit, 70 Police Mobile Force, the Nigerian Army’s 251 Tank Battalion, Forest Guards, Kogi State Vigilant

item.title: 2027: SDP’s Adamu promises free education, electricity relief for small businesses in Nasarawa
item.description: The Nasarawa State governorship candidate of the Social Democratic Party (SDP), former Inspector-General of Police, Abubakar Adamu, has promised to introduce free education in public primary and secondary schools and remove electricity bills for small-scale businesses if elected in 2027. Adamu said the proposed interventions were aimed at reducing the financial pressure on ordinary families and business owners struggling to meet basic expenses. He made the promises on Wednesday, November 18, while addressing supporters and residents of Gade community in Karu Local Government Area of the state. The former police chief said his administration would ensure that parents no longer had to struggle to pay school fees for their children. “We do not see any reason why a family, whether it is a boy or a girl, should have children in primary or secondary school and still struggle to pay school fees,” he said. “Government is supposed to take responsibility for that. Therefore, our administration will end the suffering associated with paying school fees by providing free education across primary and secondary schools.” He also pledged to remove electricity bills for small-scale business operators, arguing that the cost of power had become an additional burden for people trying to earn a living. “Insha Allah, our administration will remove the burden of electricity bills on small-scale businesses,” he said. On security, Adamu promised to deploy his experience as a former police chief to address insecurity in the state, particularly the challenges confronting farmers. He said the situation had prevented many residents from accessing their farmlands and earning a livelihood. “We are also aware that insecurity has become a major challenge. Many people can no longer go to their farms because of insecurity. If elected, we will deploy our experience to ensure that citizens enjoy the security they deserve,” he said. Adamu also criticised the administration of the All Progressives Congress (APC) in the state, asking residents to assess its performance before deciding whether to support it for another term. He warned that re-electing the ruling party would mean another eight years of hardship for residents. The SDP candidate said his decision to seek the governorship was driven by the need to improve the living conditions of ordinary people. He further asked Gade residents to nominate three representatives for his campaign council, saying they would serve as a link between the community and his team and monitor the fulfilment of promises made to them. item.title: Meet the three candidates contesting 2027 FIFA presidential election
item.description: French football chief Philippe Diallo and veteran Japanese official Kozo Tashima were on Thursday confirmed by FIFA as the challengers to incumbent Gianni Infantino in next year’s presidential election. Infantino has faced criticism over his aborted plan to allow private investment into the World Cup, but he retains considerable support for his bid to win re-election next March. French Football Federation president Diallo will represent UEFA, the European confederation which has been the most vocal in its criticism of Infantino. Tashima is a former head of the Japan Football Association and has served on the FIFA Council. FIFA said the candidacies will be examined by the body’s electoral committee before a final decision is made on whether to admit them. Ramon Vega, the Swiss former Tottenham defender who had expressed a desire to run against Infantino, was not included among the candidates. item.title: INEC backs code for independent tabulation of 2027 election results
item.description: The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) has endorsed a voluntary Code of Conduct for independent tabulation and publication of election results ahead of 2027. INEC Chairman, Prof. Joash Amupitan, gave the backing at a stakeholders’ roundtable convened by Yiaga Africa in Abuja. The Executive Director of Yiaga Africa, Samson Itodo, states this in a statement he signed on Thursday in Abuja. According to Itodo, Amupitan, who was represented by INEC’s Director of Information and Communication Technology, Dr Lawrence Bayode, said the code would strengthen transparency and public confidence. He warned that independently aggregated figures, projections and partial tallies must never be presented as official election results. “Independent verification should complement electoral accountability, not create competing centres of statutory authority,” the INEC boss stated. Amupitan outlined six guiding principles for the framework, including methodological integrity, accuracy, information integrity, data security, error accountability and voluntary compliance. Itodo said independent tabulation helps citizens to scrutinise election outcomes and assess credibility. The Yiaga Africa boss noted that differing methodologies and publication standards could cause confusion during sensitive collation periods if left uncoordinated. He stressed that a common code would establish minimum standards, curb premature declarations and ensure findings are backed by reliable verification. Itodo said Yiaga Africa was expected to lead further engagements to translate the agreed principles into a practical framework before the 2027 general elections. Participants at the forum included civil society groups, political parties, election observers, the National Broadcasting Commission and the Broadcasting Organisations of Nigeria. Also in attendance were representatives of the Nigerian Press Council (NPC) and the Nigeria Union of Journalists (NUJ). Stakeholders examined different tabulation models, including Yiaga Africa’s Processing Results Voter Tabulation (PRVT) and Election Results Analysis Dashboard (ERAD), alongside INEC’s Result Viewing Portal (IReV) aggregations. They agreed that organisations must clearly disclose their methodologies, data sources and margins of error to prevent public misinterpretation. A technical session also highlighted the need for human verification, audit trails, data security and transparent error-correction procedures. Media stakeholders emphasised the duty of journalists to verify figures and clearly distinguish independent tallies from official results declared by INEC. (NAN) The post INEC backs code for independent tabulation of 2027 election results appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Prince Harry says would rejoin military to fight Russia if needed
item.description: Britain’s Prince Harry said he would “sign up again” to serve in the military and fight against Russia if needed, in an interview from Ukraine with The Telegraph aired Thursday. “I think there’s a lot that the whole world can learn from Ukraine,” the prince said during an unannounced visit to the western city of Lviv over the weekend. “If asked to sign up again, if the need is there, then I will 100% be there to serve my country alongside my fellow veterans and service personnel.” Harry, a former British army officer and the younger son of King Charles III, made his fourth visit to Ukraine since Russia’s 2022 invasion to meet wounded veterans and medics. The prince is also the founder of the Invictus Games for wounded veterans and met athletes hoping to represent Ukraine at next year’s games in the British city of Birmingham. “Just because there’s not drones, bullets, and rockets flying at us, that doesn’t mean that we’re not at war,” he told the British daily’s “Ukraine: The Latest” podcast. “I feel very confident that Europe has a united front, and it would be fantastic to have more American support for that as well,” he added. Earlier on his weekend visit to Lviv he told wounded veterans and medics specialising in war injuries: “You’re going to win the war”. He repeated that sentiment on the podcast, insisting that “Ukraine are winning” and “there is no version where Russia is making any more advances”. The 42-year-old prince has previously spoken about being moved by witnessing death and life-changing injuries while on deployment in Afghanistan, and launched the Invictus Games in 2014 when he was still in the British army. Harry, his wife Meghan and their two children moved back to the UK earlier this year from California amid an enduring rift with the royal family and his brother and heir-to-the-throne Prince William. But the Sussex couple have launched themselves back into public life since their surprise return, carrying out engagements and visiting the EU parliament last week for an event about the dangers children face online. Despite their busy schedule, Meghan has been keeping a relatively low profile since her estranged father was charged in the US for the alleged possession of child sexual abuse images. item.title: I disobeyed my father’s order to delete succession video – Jimmy Odukoya
item.description: The Senior Pastor of The Fountain of Life Church, Jimmy Odukoya, has admitted disobeying his late father, Pastor Taiwo Odukoya, by retaining a succession video he was instructed to delete after the founder’s successful surgery in 2021. Odukoya described his decision to keep the recording as a grave mistake while addressing about 300 church workers on Wednesday, against the backdrop of the ongoing leadership crisis at the church. He explained that his father requested the recording before travelling to the United States for surgery because he feared he might not survive the procedure. According to Church Times, which reported details of the meeting, Odukoya said he personally recorded the message in which Taiwo identified Pastor Kunle Areogun as his preferred successor. However, following his successful operation, the late founder reportedly asked him to erase the recording, saying the circumstances that prompted its creation no longer applied. Rather than comply, Jimmy kept the video, a decision he now acknowledges was wrong. He also claimed that only a few people, including his sisters, knew about the recording, alleging that they were responsible for making it public. The video has become central to the leadership dispute at the church, with a faction of its Board of Trustees relying on its contents to withdraw recognition of Jimmy as Senior Pastor. The faction announced on November 17 that it had appointed Pastor Rotimi Okpaise as interim spiritual and administrative leader, citing Taiwo’s instruction that Areogun should succeed him. In the recording, the late founder said Areogun should take over if he died or became unable to communicate, while assigning Jimmy the roles of Areogun’s administrative assistant and head of the youth church. Jimmy, however, has rejected the board faction’s decision, insisting that he remains the church’s legitimate Senior Pastor and Chairman of the Board of Trustees. He told the workers that the disagreement with the board began about a year after he assumed office, when members allegedly asked him to relinquish his position as board chairman and concentrate on pastoral responsibilities. He also alleged that his sister, Pastor Tolu Odukoya-Ijogun, approached him to step aside to allow her to become board chairman. The disagreement was reportedly taken to the General Overseer of the Redeemed Christian Church of God, Pastor Enoch Adeboye, after Bishop Mike Okonkwo intervened. Jimmy further denied allegations that he misappropriated N250m donated to the church for a project, maintaining that the money remained intact and that economic challenges had delayed the project. He said he had restricted access to church funds and dismissed claims of financial misconduct. Although he maintained that he remained Senior Pastor, Jimmy expressed uncertainty about the conduct of the next Sunday service and said an advertised church programme would not hold to prevent further escalation of the dispute. item.title: ‘Grand Theft Auto VI’ Launches Worldwide To Near-Perfect Reviews
item.description: Gamers around the world got their first taste of “Grand Theft Auto VI” on Wednesday, as critics heaped praise on one of the most anticipated video game releases ever. The latest installment of the crime franchise comes 13 years after the last full edition broke sales records and became one of the most profitable entertainment products of all time. The series lets players live out gangster fantasies, smash up cars and fight whoever they choose in a fictionalized US city populated by lowlifes, sex workers and thugs. “GTA VI” launched first in New Zealand at midnight local time (1100 GMT Wednesday) and is rolling out around the world as each market reaches midnight. New Zealander Luke Starik was among the first to play, and his character did not last long. “Wasted already. First one, didn’t survive long,” he told AFP, laughing. “This is one of the big things in my life…I’ve been playing GTA for such a long time,” Riley Fennel, an Australian student visiting Tokyo, told AFP. Review aggregator Metacritic gave the game a score of 99 out of 100. A 42-year-old gamer wrote on a German-language Reddit forum that he had taken time off work to play all night. By 1:20 am, he was already in bed with a headache, still blown away by the game. “Thirteen years ago, with a game like this, I’d have played until six in the morning,” the gamer wrote. In the game’s official Reddit forum, people raved about improved interactive elements, such as being able to push a stranded ski jet back in the water. “This is amazing!” one person wrote. Analytics firm Omdia estimates “GTA VI” could generate $3.2 billion in sales by the end of the year for studio Rockstar Games and parent company Take-Two Interactive. PlayStation briefly reported connection issues on its status page before services were restored. People play Grand Theft Auto VI (GTA VI) at Bamboo Gaming Center & Bar in Bangkok on November 19, 2026, on the day of the highly anticipated video game’s release. Photo by LILLIAN SUWANRUMPHA / AFP ‘Taylor Swift of games’ In a review for The Verge titled “GTA VI does something impossible — it lives up to the hype,” Andrew Webster wrote that “the game is so good that the outsize hype is the least interesting thing about it.” Social media users praised the graphics. “There’s one moment, no spoilers, where the light hits behind one of the characters just right, and I swore I was looking at a real human,” wrote Reddit user No_Strike9652. Before the release, Joost van Dreunen, a professor at New York University’s Stern School of Business, told AFP the game was an “outlier” in the entertainment industry. “This is the Taylor Swift of video games,” he said. “The reach of the game is such that it will lead to a downstream effect on engagement on other entertainment services,” such as streaming platforms, said Omdia analyst James McWhirter. But the Sussex couple have launched themselves back into public life since their surprise return, carrying out engagements and visiting the EU parliament last week for an event about the dangers children face online. Despite their busy schedule, Meghan has been keeping a relatively low profile since her estranged father was charged in the US for the alleged possession of child sexual abuse images. item.title: South Koreans Sit Key College Exam Mired In Cheating Scandal
item.description: South Korea cut Wi-Fi around exam halls and is offering $75,000 rewards to whistleblowers in an all-out battle against AI-assisted cheating as half a million students sit their gruelling college entrance exams on Thursday. Known as the Suneung, the once-a-year, nine-hour-long exam is widely seen as a ticket to prestigious universities, well-paid jobs, and even better marriage prospects in the highly competitive country. But this year, fears of AI-assisted cheating have driven authorities to extraordinary lengths, including doubling the number of supervisors and sending random emergency alerts to detect any smartphones illegally smuggled into the exam centres. As students were still taking the test on Thursday afternoon, South Korea’s Prime Minister Han Seong-sook ordered that Suneung papers from 2025 be kept for a cheating probe. “The Ministry of Education shall maintain the current storage conditions of last year’s (college entrance exam) papers until further notice,” the PM’s office said, adding that they are normally discarded after the following year’s test. Anxious parents were earlier seen hugging their children in the South Korean capital, where temperatures dropped below zero overnight. “I came here with a heavy heart because of concerns over AI cheating,” Bang Min-ji, 18, told AFP as she prepared to enter the Yeouido Girls’ High School in central Seoul on Thursday morning. The exam kicked off at 8.40 am (2340 GMT Wednesday), with a nationwide mobile phone alert sounding 10 minutes beforehand. An AFP photographer saw a late-running student race into the high school after getting a ride in a police car. Students were told to turn up with just pencils. Erasers will be provided by the test centres, as authorities try to reduce the chances of concealed digital devices disguised as stationery. Exam-takers were also asked to avoid wearing clothes with buttons, with those who fail to comply having stickers placed over the buttons to prevent the use of hidden cameras. Bang said she feared that restrictions on writing instruments could disrupt her exam. “I’m worried I might panic if I have difficulty using the stationery provided during the test.” Elsewhere in the South Korean capital, boys were pictured with their heads in their hands as they sat nervously at exam desks. A total of 22 test-takers were found with smartphones after the morning alerts were sent, vice education minister Choi Eun-ok told a press briefing. They would be referred to exam authorities to undergo “a thorough inspection to determine whether they were carrying miniature cameras or other electronic devices”, she said. item.title: Rising political violence could threaten 2027 elections — Ndume
item.description: Senator Ali Ndume has warned that increasing political violence and intolerance could undermine the 2027 general elections, calling on security agencies and other relevant authorities to address the trend before it spreads. Ndume, who represents Borno South Senatorial District, gave the warning during an interview with Arise News on Wednesday, following the Senate’s consideration of a motion seeking investigations and prosecution of those responsible for electoral violence. The motion was sponsored by Senator Abdul Ningi, with Ndume serving as a seconder. The former Senate Chief Whip said the lawmakers were concerned about reported attacks involving President Bola Tinubu’s convoy, the presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, Peter Obi, and former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar. He said the Senate wanted authorities to intervene early to prevent political violence from becoming more widespread. “So that we may nip it in the bud,” he said. Ndume likened the situation to a fire that could become difficult to contain once it spreads. “The problem is like fire. If it catches, you don’t know why it will stop, and you may have problem putting it off,” he said. He also called for the prosecution of individuals who finance or organise attacks, insisting that responsibility should not be limited to those who carry out the violence. “If, for example, I sponsored, confirmed, evidently sponsored that group to carry out that kind of criminality, then I should be held responsible too,” he said. The senator proposed the establishment of special courts to handle electoral violence cases, arguing that delays in the justice system often allow offenders to escape accountability. “The problem with our judicial system is justice has been excessively delayed,” he said. He further urged authorities to prohibit the use of weapons, including knives and sticks, during political campaigns and ensure that those who violate the restriction face prosecution. Commenting on the security response to the reported attack on Tinubu’s convoy, Ndume commended security agencies but cautioned against comparing the President’s protection with that available to ordinary Nigerians. “You cannot compare that with the security of Mr President,” he said. He, however, stressed that protecting every citizen remained a constitutional responsibility of government, citing Section 14(2)(b) of the 1999 Constitution. Ndume also expressed disappointment over allegations that some state governors were preventing opposition parties from using public facilities for political activities. “I’m not only surprised, but I’m disappointed,” he said, describing the practice as “kind of cheap things.” He attributed the involvement of young people in political violence partly to unemployment and growing frustration, warning that anger among the youth could worsen the situation. “Violence, by youth and children, is trying to take over the political scene,” he said. item.title: Why I rejected European country posting for South Africa — Fani-Kayode
item.description: Nigeria’s High Commissioner to South Africa, Femi Fani-Kayode, has disclosed that he appealed to President Bola Tinubu to be reassigned to South Africa after he was initially posted to a European country. He made the disclosure at a dinner and reception organised by the Nigerian High Commission and Consular Office in Pretoria following the presentation of his letters of credence to South African President Cyril Ramaphosa on November 13. “I was sent here by our president, President Bola Ahmed, president of the Federal Republic of Nigeria — 250 million strong, a massive country, resilient people with rich history, very proud people, hard-working people that love life and love their country passionately, and I’ve been sent to represent those people and our government in a country which is equally resilient, hard-working, decent, civilised, with an equally rich history and heritage, as we have,” he said. Explaining his choice of South Africa, the envoy said the two countries could work together to advance the interests of the continent. “And that’s why I chose this country. I was initially posted to a European country, and I made an appeal to our president that I preferred to go to South Africa, which he graciously agreed to. So I find myself here,” he added. Fani-Kayode was initially posted as Nigeria’s ambassador to Germany before he was reassigned to South Africa in May. At the time, he said he had formally approached the then Minister of Foreign Affairs, Yusuf Tuggar, to express his reservations about the Germany posting. The former minister said he was uncomfortable with the appointment for “a number of personal reasons” and because he had spent most of his life in Europe. He also said he preferred South Africa, a country he had never visited but had considerable interest in. Ita Enang, who was initially posted to South Africa, was subsequently reassigned to Germany in Fani-Kayode’s place. Speaking about his priorities in South Africa, Fani-Kayode said he had begun addressing issues affecting Nigerians in the country since his arrival. He also described those behind xenophobic attacks as a “tiny minority”, arguing that they did not represent the majority of South Africans, whom he described as decent and accommodating.
